name: Associated Students, Inc. (ASI)
description: The Associated Students provides support to a variety of programs aimed at meeting the needs of the students of the University. The Association also serves as a vehicle for participation in the governance of the University.

name: The ASI Food Pantry
description: The ASI Food Pantry exists to provide food and basic necessities to Sac State students with financial hardships and low food security, at no cost. In addition to helping alleviate hunger within our student community, the ASI Food Pantry aims to decrease the negative impact that low food security has on the academic success of our students.

name: Basic Needs Resource Center (BNRC)
description: The BNRC is a food pantry in the Well that ensures that students don't have to choose between essentials and education! You can shop once a week, and are appointment-based for a more personalized experience.

name: Peer & Academic Resource Center
description: PARC's mission is to promote the scholastic achievements of students through enriched and supportive peer-learning opportunities that aid students along the pathway to degree attainment. PARC utilizes the talented and knowledgeable students who serve as SI Leaders, Peer Advisors and Peer Tutors.

name: Women's Resource Center (WRC)
description: The WRC cultivates a safe space where students can be empowered and affirmed. We provide various services to all students interested in learning about and supporting women-identifying students and allies. Our programming challenges sexism, socialized gender roles, and the patriarchy.

name: The Pride Center
description: The PRIDE Center provides students looking for a connection to campus with programs and events, access to resources on campus and in the community, a welcoming space, and opportunities for education about LGBTQIA communities and the intersections of many identities and experiences.

name: Disability Access Center (DAC)
description: The DAC offers support to any enrolled student who meets the standard of a qualified individual with a disability (QID), whether temporarily or permanently disabled. It strives to foster that a disability is a positive identity, and set up students for a path of independence and self-advocacy.

name: Multi-Cultural Center
description: At the Multi-Cultural Center, our mission is to foster an empowered campus that is committed to building bridges, promoting social justice, honoring diverse perspectives, and advancing social awareness and cross-cultural understanding.

name: SWANA Center
description: The SWANA Center is a welcoming space dedicated to building belonging, inclusion, and community for students with ties to the Southwest Asian and North African (SWANA) region, encompassing students identifying as Middle Eastern, North African, Arab, Amazigh, Armenian, Kurdish, Persian, and many other identities. It is also open to anyone who wishes to learn, connect, and support.

name: El Centro Serna
description: El Serna Center is dedicated to cultivating an environment that champions leadership, empowerment, self-advocacy, and civic engagement among those interested in culture, heritage, and life of Chicanx/Latinx students and those from other under-represented backgrounds at Sacramento State University.

name: APIDA Center
description: The Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) Center serves all Sacramento State community members and allies regardless of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin, who are interested in APIDA culture, heritage, and life. The Center is committed to holding space to cultivate collaboration to address the unique and diverse needs of APIDA students.

name: Career Center
description: Through a collaborative career development approach, we engage, educate and empower our students and alumni to thrive and successfully contribute to our community, economy and future workforce. We develop employer and community partnerships to recruit, collaborate with and inform our talented students and alumni.

name: College & Department Scholarships
description: The Scholarships Office at Sacramento State is dedicated to supporting students by offering a wide variety of institutional and community scholarships. The Scholarships Office awards nearly $4 million dollars in institutional scholarships each year.

name: University Reading and Writing Center
description: The primary goal of the University Reading and Writing Center (URWC) is to provide encouraging, focused, and non-judgmental one-to-one tutorials in reading and writing for any undergraduate or graduate student at CSUS. Support includes help with brainstorming, feedback on focus, organization and clarity, and one unit for regular tutoring (ENGL 121).

name: College of Education's Ed Equity Program
description: Our vision is to be the regional leader in preparing and developing excellent teachers and educators. In collaboration with local schools and communities, educators prepared at Sacramento State create and sustain equitable inclusive educational environments which are designed to optimize access and student success.

name: Pop-up Shop in Union
description: The Pop-Up Shop at the University Union is a brand new space and service where students can shop and support Sac State student business owners and makers selling their goods and services! Vendors will rotate weekly, Mondays through Fridays, 10 am - 4 pm. Shopping is open to the public.

name: Student Service Center
description: The Student Service Center serves as the central hub for student services, including enrollment, registration, financial aid, and more. Advisors and counselors are available to assist you in person, by phone, or via email.
